questions.question: How do BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link actually work together?
questions.title: React Router Fundamentals
questions.direct_answer: BrowserRouter is the context provider that reads/writes the URL via the History API — everything router-aware inside it (Routes, Link, hooks) syncs with the browser address bar. Routes is the MATCHER: given the current location, it scores every child Route's path (ranked by specificity, not order) and renders the SINGLE best match (path attribute; paths are relative to the parent Route in nesting). Route = one path→element rule: <Route path="dashboard" element={<Dashboard />} />. Link (and NavLink with active styling) is the navigation trigger — it renders an <a> with proper href (middle-click, cmd-click, SEO all work) but calls preventDefault and pushes through the router instead of a full page load, so the SPA stays mounted.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    BR[BrowserRouter: History API provider] --> LOC[current location context]
    LOC --> RT[Routes: score every child Route]
    RT --> RANK[static > dynamic :id > splat * — specificity ranking, not order]
    RANK --> ONE[render the single best-matching element]
    LK[Link: real a href + intercepted click] -->|push| LOC
    NL[NavLink: Link + isActive styling] --> LK
    A['<a href> internal'] -.full reload: state dies.-> BAD
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The state-preservation economics (why SPA routing exists): every full navigation re-downloads/re-executes the app — auth context, theme, in-progress form state, and data caches vanish. Router navigation keeps the React tree mounted; only the matched subtree swaps. That's also the gotcha: REMATCHING resets route-level component state (a search form inside a route remounts when its params change) — the fix is either keyed persistence, moving state up, or search params (useSearchParams) as the durable state.

Nested routing and Outlet (the v6 composition model): a Route with children renders its element + an <Outlet /> placeholder where the child match renders. Path RELATIVITY follows: a child Route path="settings" inside path="dashboard" matches /dashboard/settings without repeating the prefix — and ranking composes the same way. useParams exposes the dynamic segments at any level. This is how layout routes work: a pathless Route (<Route element={<Shell />}> with no path) contributes layout without consuming URL segments — the standard sidebar/nav-shell pattern.

The data APIs worth naming (v6.4+, now loaders/actions): createBrowserRouter + RouterProvider replaced BrowserRouter for the data-router feature set — loaders fetch before render (the route owns its data), actions handle mutations, useNavigation exposes the pending state (the standard 'loading UI without waterfalls'), and useFetcher submits without navigating. The honest summary: BrowserRouter/Routes is the pure-render model every codebase has; the data router is the current recommendation for new work — same matching engine, richer contract.
